Delivery Hero treats the pre-August 2021 model as a probable risk and the post-August 2021 model as merely possible.

- For the model operated by Glovo until August 2021, the risk is "more likely than not," so appropriate provisions are recognized in the Consolidated Financial Statements (Strategic Risks, [2]).
- For the model since August 2021, the risk is deemed possible but not probable, so it is disclosed as a contingency — a contingent liability of €440 to 770 million for social security claims (Strategic Risks [2]; Contingencies note 5 [1], [6]).
- No provision has been recognized for the post-2021 model because reclassification by Spanish courts was assessed as not probable (Note 5, [6]).
- For the old model, Glovo had to provide bank guarantees to Spanish courts in 2024 to secure claimed liabilities (Strategic Risks, [3], [4]).
- Glovo decided in December 2024, effective 2025, to progressively move to an employment-based model in Spain to avoid further legal uncertainties, while defending the self-employed status in ongoing proceedings (Strategic Risks, [3]; Business development by segment, [5]).

Zalando - end of 2022: EUR 106.5m committed
Zalando - end of 2024: 59.5m EUR committed

The commitment fell by 47.0m EUR (106.5m − 59.5m) between the end of 2022 and the end of 2024.
Approximately 850,000 riders worldwide delivered at least one order for Delivery Hero in 2024.

Zalando changed Zalando Plus in 2024 from a paid membership to a free-to-join model with a points-based system rewarding customer loyalty, and its report mentions increased accruals for the reimbursement of Zalando Plus subscription fees to customers at the beginning of 2025, included in "others" among other current non-financial liabilities.

- The programme became free-to-join, with points earned through purchases and activities like newsletter subscriptions unlocking four benefit levels (Group strategy, [1]; Key intangible resources, [3]).
- It was initially tested in Spain and expanded to France and Austria in 2024, with further rollout planned for 2025 ([1], [6]).
- The awards create a separate performance obligation providing a material right to customers (Accounting policies, [2]).
- The year-end accrual for reimbursing Zalando Plus subscription fees at the start of 2025 is included in "others" within other current non-financial liabilities (Notes (9.-26.), [5]).

Vodafone Turkey - 2G licence extension: €120 million for a six-year extension (excluding 18% VAT), paid in advance with a capital injection, with the extension agreement signed effective as of 27 April 2023.
Turkcell - 2G licence extension: EUR 120 million (plus EUR 21.6 million of value-added taxes), paid in installments — an initial payment of EUR 81.6 million (TRY 1.7 billion) during 2023, approximately half of the remaining installments (EUR 31.1 million, TRY 1.1 billion) in April 2024, with the remaining amount to be paid within a year.

Both agreed to the same €120 million fee, but Vodafone Turkey paid it in advance via a capital injection, whereas Turkcell paid in installments in Turkish Lira over time.
